html:
A play by the Norwegian writer Henrik Ibsen, first staged in Copenhagen in December 1879. It is one of the founding works of modern realist drama.

Nora Helmer seems to live a happy life with her husband Torvald, who treats her like a pretty pet. Years before, to save his life, she secretly borrowed money by forging her father's signature. When the secret comes out, Torvald turns on her, then forgives her once the danger passes. Nora sees that he never loved her as an equal. She tells him she must learn who she is, and walks out on him and her children. The play ends with the slam of the door.

The ending shocked audiences. One German actress refused to play it, and Ibsen wrote a second ending in which Nora stays for the children. The play became a rallying point for the women's movement, though Ibsen said it was about being human. Its plain everyday speech and its focus on a marriage changed theatre, and it is one of the most performed plays in the world.
